texts.313d468c6997: Thus far only retrospective data has been available to assess this. Although most breast cancer recurrences occur during the first ten years of follow-up, late recurrence is well recognised as late toxic effects from breast cancer treatment. The latter are of particular interest in this cohort of unusually young breast cancer patients. The study aims to determine whether genetic factors are important in determining short and long term outcomes after breast cancer treatment. The study is a prospective observational cohort study. Annual follow up forms are sent to the recruiting hospital. Once patients pass five years from treatment without relapse we wish to target the collection of data to patients who have relapsed or developed new cancers. When notified of a new cancer diagnosis we will contact the recruiting hospital for information about site of disease, pathology and treatment. Currently we rely on annual follow up forms to capture relapse events, if this becomes possible via MRIS then this would further facilitate our aims. Cancer specific and all cause mortality are defined end points for the study.
